sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: London Stadium hosts West Ham (18th, 36 points) against leaders Arsenal (1st, 76). Sofascore model: home 13%, draw 18%, away 69%; both teams to score 53%. West Ham need points for safety, Arsenal are targeting another decisive step in the title race.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: West Ham are 2-2-1 across 5, mixing a 4-0 over Wolverhampton and a 0-0 at Crystal Palace with a 0-3 loss at Brentford. Arsenal are 3-1-1, with 3 clean sheets and strong underlying numbers (xG 3.23 v Fulham, 1.56 v Atlético Madrid). Momentum favours the visitors.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: The last 2 meetings at Arsenal ended 2-0 to Arsenal and 1-0 to West Ham. Across the last 5 head-to-heads the away side have 3 wins to 2. Bukayo Saka has excelled recently (average rating 8.22, 4 goals, 2 assists).

sections.subtitle: Season stats and playing styles
sections.text: West Ham’s profile: low possession (42.7%), high defensive workload (interceptions 9.3 per game, 1st) and threat in transition (fast breaks 1.29 per game, 3rd), but 61 conceded (18th defence). Arsenal pair efficiency at both ends (67 scored, 26 conceded) with Declan Rice’s supply (62 key passes, 16 big chances created) and wide quality from Bukayo Saka and Leandro Trossard. Viktor Gyökeres’ recent output (3 goals, 1 assist in 5) adds penalty-box presence.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Chris Kavanagh averages 3.7 yellows per match (reds 0.12). West Ham average 1.8 yellows, and both teams trend to under 4.5 cards; corners have stayed under 10.5 in most recent matches. Expect roughly 3 bookings and about 9 total corners.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Arsenal’s form, defensive record and recent head-to-head edge align with the model’s 69% away-win probability. With both teams to score at 53%, West Ham have a fair chance to register, but Arsenal are the more reliable side to take the points.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Goalless at the break at London Stadium, but the pattern has been clear. Arsenal have controlled territory and possession, while West Ham United have looked to break quickly and protect their box. The visitors have created the better openings but lacked composure with their finishing.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal asserted control after the opening minutes, building a long sustained attacking spell around the 10–15 minute period and keeping West Ham pinned back for much of the half. A further steady attacking phase followed through the mid-half. West Ham’s most notable response arrived late, with brief counters around the mid-30s and a final push just before the interval that hinted at their transition threat.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key first-half stats
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal lead most metrics: possession 66%, expected goals 0.79 vs 0.14, big chances 3 vs 1, shots on target 2 vs 1, penalty area entries 11 vs 5, and final third entries 27 vs 23. They also hit the woodwork twice. West Ham have competed well in duels (54% won) but have struggled to sustain attacks, with limited entries into dangerous areas.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical patterns
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal’s width and rotations have stretched West Ham’s back line, with Leandro Trossard the most threatening, responsible for multiple big chances and shots on target. Service from Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka has consistently found advanced runners. West Ham’s plan has been compact and direct, looking for Jarrod Bowen and Crysencio Summerville on the break, while Aaron Wan-Bissaka produced their clearest opening with a key pass leading to the missed big chance. The hosts’ defensive line has cleared danger effectively, but Arsenal’s repeat entries suggest pressure may tell if the tempo is maintained.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Discipline and set pieces
halftimeSections.text: West Ham have 2 yellow cards (Crysencio Summerville, Valentín Castellanos); Arsenal have none. Corners stand at 1–2. With West Ham defending deep and likely absorbing more pressure, another home booking is a reasonable risk. Arsenal’s corner count could rise if they continue to force blocks and recoveries in wide areas.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: If Arsenal keep the ball speed high and continue to attack the half-spaces, the breakthrough should come. West Ham’s route is via quicker outlets and earlier support to the first pass in transition; they need more penalty area entries to turn counters into shots. The late surge from the hosts shows there is space to exploit if Arsenal overcommit, but the visitors remain favourites to score first given chance volume and territory.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal to make their pressure count after the interval, with Trossard the most likely to convert. West Ham will have moments on the counter, but the balance of chances points to a narrow away win. Predicted next goal: Arsenal. Predicted final score: West Ham United 0–1 Arsenal.
